jobs.description:
Overview
The IP Group (IPG) is seeking a Technical Program Manager to support the execution, coordination, and operational readiness of business-critical technology initiatives across engineering, security, compliance, operations, and business teams.

In this role, you will work closely with senior technical, program, and business leaders to translate established priorities into actionable plans and help coordinate activities across multiple technical workstreams. You will support program planning and tracking, security and compliance activities, operational readiness, release coordination, vendor engagement, documentation, risk and dependency management, and stakeholder communication.

This position is well suited for an organized and technically capable program manager who enjoys working across teams, bringing structure to complex initiatives, and helping technical and business stakeholders move work forward. You will provide the coordination, visibility, and follow-through needed to support reliable technology operations and successful delivery of approved initiatives.

The role is focused on execution and operational support rather than ownership of portfolio strategy or long-term program direction. You will partner with senior leaders and technical owners to help ensure priorities are effectively coordinated, risks and dependencies remain visible, and technical, operational, security, and compliance commitments progress toward completion.

Responsibilities
As a Technical Program Manager supporting IPG Technical Operations, you will provide program management, coordination, and execution support for business-critical technology initiatives across engineering, security, compliance, operations, and business teams.
Key responsibilities include:
- Support the execution of technical programs and initiatives by helping translate established priorities into actionable plans, milestones, dependencies, risks, and measurable outcomes.
- Coordinate activities across engineering, business operations, security, compliance, and other technical stakeholders to help programs progress from requirements through implementation, testing, release, and operational handoff.
- Maintain project plans, schedules, backlogs, risks, dependencies, decisions, and delivery status, identifying potential issues and coordinating with appropriate owners on resolution or escalation.
- Support the operational health and readiness of IPG applications, platforms, and technical services by coordinating deployments, releases, service improvements, incident follow-up, and remediation activities.
- Assist technical and program owners with execution of security, privacy, risk, and compliance requirements, including vulnerability remediation, technical assessments, audit and compliance actions, SFI/S360 commitments, threat-model reviews, penetration-testing follow-up, and related evidence and reporting.
- Facilitate requirements definition, backlog refinement, sprint planning, user acceptance testing, production-readiness reviews, releases, and operational transitions in partnership with engineering and business stakeholders.
- Track technical debt, security findings, operational improvements, compliance obligations, and other commitments, providing visibility to owners and stakeholders and supporting timely completion.
- Coordinate activities performed by vendors, contractors, and external delivery partners, including deliverables, schedules, dependencies, access requirements, knowledge transfer, and operational readiness.
- Develop and maintain program documentation, operational procedures, runbooks, decision records, and knowledge repositories that support service continuity and effective technology operations.
- Support established communication and operating rhythms by preparing status reporting, risk and dependency assessments, executive summaries, meeting materials, and decision-support information.
- Identify opportunities to improve execution, operational processes, documentation, automation, and service readiness, and work with appropriate owners to evaluate and implement improvements.
- Partner with senior technical, program, and business leaders to support execution of approved priorities with appropriate visibility, coordination, accountability, and follow-through.

- 1+ year(s) of experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects.

The mission of the Microsoft CISO Organization is to defend Microsoft, our customers, and our partners from cybersecurity threats. The CISO Operations Security Implementation & Capability (OSIC) team plays a critical role in turning the CISO strategy into reality. OSIC is responsible for scaling, systematizing, and operationalizing cybersecurity initiatives across the CISO Organization and across Microsoft. OSIC ensures that cybersecurity programs are well-designed, consistently executed, measurable, and sustainable at Microsoft’s global scale.

Role Overview

We are seeking a Principal Technical Program Manager to join our CISO Operations Security Implementation & Capability (OSIC) team. You will lead complex, cross-organizational cybersecurity programs from problem definition and planning through execution, adoption, and measurable outcomes. You will translate strategic priorities into clear program plans, operating mechanisms, governance, roadmaps, and success measures; use AI, telemetry, and other evidence to improve decisions and delivery; and manage priorities, risks, dependencies, and tradeoffs amid ambiguity. You will partner with technical, business, and senior leadership stakeholders to build alignment, remove blockers, and drive accountability. Your work will establish repeatable capabilities that strengthen CISO operations and scale effective practices across Microsoft.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. - Translate CISO strategic priorities into executable programs by framing problems, defining outcomes and success measures, establishing governance, mapping dependencies, and creating clear roadmaps and delivery plans.

- Build repeatable processes, automated workflows, and reusable program mechanisms that improve execution across participating teams and can be adopted by adjacent programs.

jobs.title: Technical Program Manager, Cross-Company AI Data
jobs.description:
Overview
At Microsoft AI, we are building advanced AI systems that help people and organizations achieve more. We are creating a trusted, repeatable system that turns high-value Microsoft product data into compliant, secure, researcher-ready assets for AI training and evaluation while protecting users and honoring product commitments.

This individual-contributor role sits within the Microsoft AI Lab and drives the day-to-day technical program work required to move high-value data from request through compliant acquisition, preparation, access, use, and refresh. We’re looking for an experienced Technical Program Manager who can coordinate across research, product, engineering, legal, privacy, security, Responsible AI, and data operations teams to keep complex data programs moving.

You will own execution across the data lifecycle: clarifying researcher requirements, identifying accountable source owners, ensuring data is properly obtained and approved, coordinating secure transfer and access, overseeing scrubbing and quality validation, documenting permitted uses and controls, and maintaining reliable refresh and deletion processes. You will manage technical relationships across teams, surface risks early, and unblock dependencies so approved data reaches researchers in a usable and compliant form.

The ideal candidate is a hands-on, low-ego operator who brings structure to ambiguous technical and compliance workflows, builds trust across organizational boundaries, and drives issues to resolution without relying on formal authority. They communicate clearly, maintain accurate operating records, and create repeatable mechanisms that improve delivery speed, data quality, and control adherence.

This role is based in Redmond, WA or Mountain View, CA. You are required to be in the office 4 days per week.

Responsibilities
- Drive data programs from intake through delivery by translating researcher needs into clear requirements, milestones, owners, dependencies, risks, and acceptance criteria.

- Unblock acquisition and access by coordinating with product data owners, engineering teams, legal, privacy, security, Responsible AI, procurement, and external partners; escalate decisions with concise context and recommended paths.

- Manage day-to-day technical relationships with source teams and data partners, including data specifications, transfer methods, schemas, storage, access patterns, service expectations, issue resolution, and refresh commitments.

- Ensure data is properly obtained, documented, and used within approved purposes and restrictions by maintaining evidence of source, authorization, provenance, lineage, consent or opt-out requirements, retention, deletion, and access controls.

- Coordinate data preparation and remediation, including ingestion, scrubbing, de-identification, credential and PII removal, deduplication, filtering, quality checks, and validation against researcher requirements and compliance controls.

- Oversee recurring refreshes and lifecycle operations by defining schedules, monitoring freshness and delivery health, resolving failures, validating replacement datasets, and ensuring expired or disallowed data is removed as required .

- Maintain clear program artifacts and operating rhythms, including status, decisions, risks, control evidence, issue logs, handoffs, and metrics for cycle time, quality, refresh reliability, compliance, and researcher readiness.

Qualifications
Required Qualifications

- Bachelor’s Degree AND 6+ years of experience in engineering, product or technical program management, data operations, privacy-sensitive technology, or equivalent experience.

- Experience driving complex, cross-organizational technical programs with multiple dependencies, clear milestones, risk management, and measurable delivery outcomes.

- Experience working with data pipelines or lifecycle operations, including acquisition, ingestion, transformation, quality validation, access, refresh, retention, and deletion.

- Demonstrated ability to influence without authority, build productive technical relationships, resolve ambiguous ownership, and communicate decisions and escalations clearly.

- Working knowledge of AI training and evaluation data and relevant controls, including privacy, data protection, IP and licensing, security, Responsible AI, consent, provenance, lineage, access restrictions, de-identification, and permitted use.

Preferred Qualifications

- Bachelor’s Degree AND 8+ years of experience in engineering, product or technical program management, AI data operations, data governance, privacy-sensitive products, or equivalent experience.

- Experience delivering data programs across product , research, engineering, legal, privacy, security, Responsible AI, and platform teams in a large or highly regulated environment.

- Strong technical judgment and written communication skills, with experience defining operational controls, troubleshooting data delivery issues, creating scalable processes, and using metrics to improve cycle time, quality, compliance, and refresh reliability.

Working across research, Azure engineering, product teams, suppliers, and external partners, you will translate product scenarios into clear requirements, specifications, verification plans, and technical roadmaps, while driving trade-offs and risk management across optics, electronics, packaging, thermal, mechanical, firmware, networking, manufacturing, and qualification.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.

- Act as a primary technical interface with suppliers and development partners, ensuring deliverables are complete, testable, and aligned to specification.
- Partner with Microsoft Research, Azure engineering, product, supply-chain, and operations teams to maintain an integrated product and technology roadmap.

- Experience defining requirements, specifications, interfaces, verification plans, or qualification criteria for a complex multidisciplinary hardware or infrastructure product.

- Demonstrated ability to provide strong execution leadership across teams while retaining ownership of product definition and system-level technical outcomes.
